name: Space Within the Central Channel
previous_vbt_ref: VBT dharana 012 (Singh-style sequential method index; commonly verse 35) (superseded)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: madhyanāḍī madhyasaṃsthā bisasūtrābharūpayā | dhyātāntarvyomayā devyā tayā devaḥ prakāśate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
dharana.rendering: The central channel stands in the middle, slender as the fibre in a lotus stalk; when it is meditated on as the Goddess whose nature is the inner sky, through her the God shines forth.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: meditate on the inner vacuity of the medial channel, which he identifies as the suṣumnā; the verse itself says only 'in the middle'.

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y9 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 35 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: a filament-thin channel through the middle of the body
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one very fine channel running through the middle of the body, felt as open inner space rather than as something to grip.
geometry.svg_hint: a hair-thin vertical line through the centre of the body, hollow inside
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Line open
reaction.summary: School metaphor: a crowded sense of the body thins into one fine, open channel, like a filament lighting up. Not a medical or biochemical claim.

breath.lands_in: ordinary breath; the channel is felt, not breathed into
breath.cue: Equal four-count breath if counting helps, otherwise natural. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Orient to the exact middle of the body
orientation.gravity: Body supported; no muscular lifting of the spine
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: A slender channel through the middle of the body, sensed as open inner space
attention.secondary: The quiet of that inner space

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: The central channel stands in the middle, slender as the fibre in a lotus stalk; when it is meditated on as the Goddess whose nature is the inner sky, through her the God shines forth.
adiyogi.method_summary: Rest awareness on one continuous slender channel through the middle of the body, fine as a lotus-stalk fibre, and feel its inside as open space rather than as a muscle to grip. No forcing of breath or effort.

honesty.disclosure: Door 012 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 12 (verse 35) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 012 is dharana 12, verse 35. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.

legacy.disclosure: Linking [retired posture] with VBT method 012 is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not an ancient one-to-one claim. The shared image is a slender line of attention (side body in [retired posture]; central filament in the verse).
legacy.notes: VBT method indexing differs by edition. This door follows Singh-style sequential dharana count from the first technique verse (about 24), so dharana 012 is approximately verse 35 (madhya-nadi / lotus-filament). Wallis groups early breath verses as one yukti, so his Y12 is a later verse. Some public dharana lists label a different sensory-Bhairava method as number 12. Guardians should keep the Singh-style school index unless the school standardizes otherwise.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If the image brings strong sensations or agitation, open the eyes and feel the whole body resting on the floor. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: Shorten the stance, rest the lower hand on a block or shin, and keep the gaze neutral if balance, neck, or hamstrings complain. General practice caution only; not medical advice.
legacy_notes.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain in hamstring, knee, sacroiliac joint, or neck.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 012: space within the central channel. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 12, verse 35.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any easy seat, or lie down. The map is one fine channel through the middle of the body.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Body supported. Eyes closed or lowered. Orient to the exact middle.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath, or four in, four out. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Feel a channel as fine as a lotus fibre through the centre. Sense its inside as open space.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a crowded body-sense thins into one open channel. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 35: the central channel, fine as a lotus fibre, meditated on as the Goddess of inner sky; through her the God shines. Space, not force.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the channel go. Feel the whole body again. Open the eyes.
